title: Core-based Hierarchies for Efficient GraphRAG

problem.claim: Vector-based retrieval methods often fail at global sensemaking tasks requiring reasoning across many documents.

gap.claim: Leiden-based GraphRAG communities can be inherently non-reproducible on sparse knowledge graphs because modularity optimization admits exponentially many near-optimal partitions.

contributions.claim: A deterministic, density-aware GraphRAG hierarchy based on k-core decomposition, with linear-time construction.
Lightweight heuristics for constructing size-bounded, connectivity-preserving communities from the k-core hierarchy.
A token-budget-aware sampling strategy intended to reduce LLM costs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The methods were evaluated on financial earnings transcripts, news articles, and podcasts using three LLMs for answer generation and five independent LLM judges for head-to-head evaluation.
Across datasets and models, the authors report improved answer comprehensiveness and diversity together with reduced token usage.

narrative_sequence.summary: RAG enhances language models by incorporating external knowledge.
Vector retrieval often struggles with global sensemaking across many documents.
GraphRAG uses recursively summarized hierarchical communities, but Leiden-based community detection is described as non-reproducible on sparse knowledge graphs.
The paper replaces Leiden with k-core decomposition and adds community-construction heuristics plus token-aware sampling.
The authors report improvements in answer comprehensiveness and diversity with lower token usage across the evaluated settings.

source_observation.claim: A deterministic structural decomposition may address reproducibility concerns in hierarchical graph organization.

interpretation.claim: When a clustering objective has many near-optimal solutions, using a deterministic graph structure can make downstream communities more stable.

application.claim: Consider deterministic decompositions such as k-core structure when building reproducible graph-based retrieval hierarchies.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether determinism improves answer quality independently of the other proposed heuristics and sampling strategy.

source_observation.claim: The reported evaluation links hierarchical community construction and token-aware sampling with improved answer characteristics and lower token usage.

interpretation.claim: Retrieval structure and budget-aware selection can jointly affect both answer quality and inference cost.

application.claim: Evaluate retrieval systems with quality and resource-use measures together when global context is expensive to process.

exception.claim: The abstract does not provide quantitative effect sizes or isolate the contribution of each component.

unknowns: Exact improvements in comprehensiveness, diversity, and token usage are not reported.
Dataset sizes, baselines, prompts, and evaluation protocols are not specified.
Ablation results for k-core decomposition, community heuristics, and sampling are not provided.
